analysis.title: USA: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson Says Future Adjustments Require “Carefully Examining Trends,” Hinting at an October Pause
key_insights: Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on 1 October 2026 that any future policy adjustments should be determined by carefully examining trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.

Jefferson said yields across the term structure have increased further since the September FOMC meeting, a sign investors are reassessing the macro landscape. He said his colleagues and he will need to come to their own judgment, which may take more time.
Jefferson supported the September rate hike as a step to keep longer-term inflation expectations anchored and to validate public confidence in the 2 percent objective.
New York Fed President John Williams said earlier this week that after the September action there is no need for urgency and the Fed has time to gather more information.

Jefferson remains concerned that higher energy prices could lead to a persistent rise in inflation more broadly. He said AI-related demand is driving unusually strong increases in the cost of producing related goods and services, boosting core inflation.

Jefferson noted that most measures of longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable at levels consistent with 2 percent. He said there are not yet spillovers from tariffs, energy price shocks, and the surge in certain goods prices into broader and more persistent inflation.

GS views Jefferson's comments as consistent with its view that an October hike is now unlikely. GS still expects the second hike in December and sees a strong chance the FOMC will conclude additional hikes are unnecessary.
After the previous day's inflation data and Williams's comments, GS pushed back its second-hike forecast to December.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects the Fed to pause at the October meeting after the September hike.
GS moved its second hike from an earlier meeting to December. It sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes further hikes are unnecessary.

macro_indicators.reading: Stable at levels consistent with 2 percent (per Jefferson)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Stable expectations support a patient Fed and argue against a faster hiking pace.

risk_factors: Higher energy prices leading to a persistent rise in broader inflation.
AI-related demand driving unusually strong cost increases for related goods and services, lifting core inflation.
Possible spillovers from tariffs, energy price shocks, and surging prices in certain goods categories into broader inflation, which Jefferson says are not yet visible.
vol_and_positioning: Yields across the term structure have risen further since the September FOMC meeting, per Jefferson.

tension_points.bull_case: Longer-term inflation expectations remain stable at levels consistent with 2 percent, and Jefferson sees no spillovers yet into broader inflation. This supports a pause in October and a possible end to hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Jefferson remains concerned that higher energy prices could drive persistent broader inflation, and that AI-related demand is lifting core inflation. GS still expects a second hike in December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of spillovers from tariffs, energy shocks, and goods prices into broader and more persistent inflation, or a rise in longer-term inflation expectations, would undercut the pause view.

theme_stances.key_argument: Jefferson's and Williams's comments are consistent with an October hike being unlikely.
theme_stances.evidence: an October hike is now unlikely
